items.title: This is what 84 cameras reveal about survival and sacrifice at Bondi
items.description: As gunshots rang out at Bondi, dozens of eyewitnesses risked their lives to film the horror. This is what they wanted you to see.

items.title: Locked and loaded, now gathering dust: What killed Narrabri's battery?
items.description: A community battery project three years in the making, run by a local not-for-profit and backed by the council, was killed after a spark of misinformation about its fire risk was ignited.

items.title: How a 20yo living with his parents allegedly plotted a terror attack
items.description: History was made in WA when police charged a person for the first time with preparing a terrorist attack. What do we know?

items.title: 'They raiding us': How nosy neighbour led police to $1b drug stash
items.description: Four masked men are arrested breaking into a Ryde apartment in Sydney's north. What officers stumbled upon inside would be one of the biggest cocaine hauls in NSW Police history.

items.title: Once-in-a-generation deluge for SA and Vic as north eyes triple cyclone threat
items.description: Populated regions stretching from Eyre Peninsula to western Victoria and the Murray River are at risk of dangerous flash flooding, amid growing signs three additional tropical lows will form off Australia's northern coast next week.

items.title: If the 'Andrew problem' remains, an almighty challenge awaits Prince William
items.description: When Prince William and Princess Catherine stepped out for their first public appearance since Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's arrest, an innocuous question was levelled at them. The candid response was perhaps more revealing than anticipated.

items.title: Why a full-scale war between the Afghan Taliban and Pakistan is unlikely
items.description: Pakistan's declaration of an "open war" with the Afghan Taliban sounds dangerous, but analysts say neither side has the capacity to win.

items.title: Advocates fear people like Graham are caught in Australia's next Robodebt
items.description: Graham Crossan cannot eat, talk or breathe unassisted but he's been denied funding for high-level care due to a new way of assessing aged care funding.

items.title: Clinton tells Congress he had 'no inkling' of Epstein's crimes
items.description: The former US president is being questioned by the House Oversight Committee, which is looking into the US government's handling of the Epstein case.

items.title: Warning financial abuse among First Nations elders a hidden problem
items.description: Experts are warning elders are suffering in silence and are calling for more awareness around financial abuse to understand how it manifests within families and communities.

items.title: Will Coles' bruising court battle be worth it?
items.description: Coles decided this bruising court battle was worth it and now a federal court judge is weighing up the evidence to decide whether that decision was a masterstroke or a massive error.

items.title: The A-League's hottest striker ready for breakthrough Matildas moment
items.description: Four years on from her first Asian Cup, Holly McNamara begins her second in career-best form. The 23-year-old has her eyes on the ultimate prize.

items.title: 'They're going to find me': Destanee Aiava on threats, racism and quitting tennis
items.description: Destanee Aiava was once called the best 14-year-old female tennis player in the world. Just over a decade later, she is walking away from the sport and calling out its toxic culture.

items.title: Can the most exploitative reality TV show actually be held accountable?
items.description: America's Next Top Model has aged terribly. What does accountability even mean for an era of unprecedented exploitation on screen?

items.title: The 11 books our critics couldn't put down this summer
items.description: Wondering what to read next? Buzzy debuts, gripping thrillers and lyrical literary fiction are among our critics' latest recommendations.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of Mad Men, musicals and weird punctuation
items.description: Every question has only two options: One is right and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: 'We exist everywhere': Why these regional towns are holding Mardi Gras parties
items.description: How do you celebrate the annual Mardi Gras parade if you live hundreds of kilometres from Sydney? These regional areas are celebrating Pride in their own special way.

items.title: Israel's top court allows aid groups to keep working in Gaza, for now
items.description: Israel's Supreme Court on Friday temporarily blocked the government from shuttering the Gaza operations of dozens of aid organisations.

items.title: SA Greens unfazed by polling, sticking to their guns on AUKUS
items.description: Ahead of the SA election, the Greens have made only modest gains in polling compared to rival minor parties, but party leader Robert Simms is not disappointed by the result.

items.title: Deputy chief of army warns ADF 'detached' from violent nature of war
items.description: Major General Chris Smith delivered an excoriating address to a major conference last year, declaring "managerial and advertising logic and double speak" had "polluted" the military.

items.title: 'Smoky scent': The novel plan to return native bush rats to Sydney
items.description: Conservationists hope a smelly plan to reintroduce Australian bush rats into a nature reserve in Sydney this weekend could help repair urban ecosystems.

items.title: New professional soccer league delivers big dreams for Pacific nations
items.description: A new professional soccer league has launched across Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific, though questions remain over whether it can survive long-term.

items.title: Liberal Party won't publish its review into disastrous 2025 election
items.description: The review received hundreds of submissions and was finished months ago, but today the Liberal Party's federal executive revealed it would never be made public.

items.title: Lighthouse keeper's wife's remains saved from being swallowed by sea
items.description: The bones of a Queensland lighthouse keeper's wife were almost lost as a result of rising sea levels nearly 150 years after her death.

items.title: Deadline looms for farmers refusing transmission line work on properties
items.description: Landholders opposed to VNI West have been given 30 days to allow environmental assessments before authorised officers can enter by force.
